input.title: Apple announces American Manufacturing Program partners for latest iPhone lineup
input.originalSummary: Apple announced new and expanded partnerships with American companies that are supplying critical materials and components for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro. Last year, the company deepened that commitment by launching AMP, aimed at bringing even more advanced manufacturing and critical component production to the United States as part of Apple’s $600 billion, four-year commitment to U.S. manufacturing and innovation. That footprint continues to grow, empowering partners across the country to bring new capabilities online: Broadcom is expanding and modernizing its Fort Collins, Colorado, facility under a $1.5 billion capital investment announced in July, producing advanced radio frequency components for a wide range of Apple products. The multiyear agreement will produce more than 15 billion U.S.-made chips.

input.title: Marvell Bolsters Connectivity Portfolio with New 3.2T Protocol-aware Retimer and Second-generation 1.6T AEC DSP
input.originalSummary: Scaling connectivity to 3.2T: Marvell® Alaska® E 3.2T protocol-aware Ethernet, UALink™ and ESUN retimer delivers 16 lanes of 224G PAM4 connectivity for high-bandwidth XPU-to-XPU and XPU-to-switch scale-up architectures. Advancing 200G/lane AECs: Second-generation Alaska A 1.6T AEC DSP moves to the 3nm node, delivering higher performance and improved power efficiency for 1.6T active electrical cables used across AI racks. Availability: Alaska E 3.2T protocol-aware retimer and second-generation Alaska A 1.6T are now sampling to customers. Together, the new 3nm devices expand the Marvell portfolio of retimer and DSP solutions for scale-up infrastructure, giving data center operators greater flexibility to optimize their infrastructure to maximize bandwidth, reach and power efficiency.

input.title: ADDING and REPLACING Marvell Unveils Second-generation Structera X, Industry-first Six-channel CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders for AI Inference
input.originalSummary: Expanding memory capacity for AI: Second-generation Marvell® Structera™ X 3406 and 3506 CXL 3.2 memory expanders add six DDR4/DDR5 channels (50% more than the prior generation) and PCIe Gen 6 connectivity, supporting up to 9TB of DDR4 or 6TB of DDR5 per controller. Preview and availability: Demoing at the OCP Summit, the Structera X 3406 and 3506 are expected to sample in Q1 2027, extending the Structera X 2404 and 2504 architecture already shipping to hyperscalers. The Marvell CXL ecosystem continues to expand across the full data center stack through close partnership with CPU and memory vendors, OEMs, ODMs and system integrators. In the near future, these same managers will use CXL’s memory pools to reduce stranded memory and drive greater savings, and they will find controllers that offer compression, as this one does, to be even more interesting.
